assertions.description: The pre-modes base grammar still parses: scroll-marker-group accepts the position keyword 'after' (shipped Chrome 135).
The parser accepts a mode keyword after a position keyword: 'scroll-marker-group: after tabs' is valid per the Chrome 154 grammar none | [ [ before | after ] || [ links | tabs ] ].
The parser accepts the explicit default mode after a position keyword: 'scroll-marker-group: before links'.
The || combinator lets the position be omitted, so the mode keyword alone is grammatically valid: 'scroll-marker-group: tabs'.
The || combinator allows either keyword order, so 'scroll-marker-group: tabs after' is grammatically valid.
Two keywords from the same || component are invalid and must be rejected: setting 'before after' via setProperty leaves the inline property empty.
Computed value is the specified keyword(s): an element with 'scroll-marker-group: after tabs' round-trips both keywords through getComputedStyle.

In tabs mode the ::scroll-marker-group exposes role tablist, markers expose role tab with roving tabindex (one tab stop, arrow keys), originating elements gain role tabpanel, and inactive panel content is pruned from the accessibility tree; in links mode the group is a navigation landmark of sequential link tab stops.
assertions.test: Pseudo-element accessibility roles and focusgroup keyboard behavior are not observable from page JavaScript; parser acceptance of the keywords does not prove them. Verify with the DevTools Accessibility pane (or an AX-tree dump) on a marker group declared 'after tabs' versus 'after links', and count keyboard tab stops by hand.
